gu-04NE.title: Pole: thick concrete poles
gu-04NE.summary: Utility poles are almost always concrete and often very thick. The Northern Mariana Islands usually have wooden poles.

gu-59r8.title: Landscape: flat northern half
gu-59r8.summary: The northern half of the island is mostly flat.

gu-793A.title: Road: lots of road reflectors
gu-793A.summary: Roads often have a very large number of road reflectors. The Northern Mariana Islands do too, so this does not separate them.

gu-D0Zu.title: Houses: white resort, orange tiled roofs
gu-D0Zu.summary: A resort complex with white buildings and orange tiled roofs. It looks a bit like tiled roofs seen in Java.

gu-Gyzt.title: Sign: green street name signs
gu-Gyzt.summary: Street name signs are green. The Northern Mariana Islands use blue ones instead.

gu-I0mE.title: Coverage: limited, almost none inland south
gu-I0mE.summary: Coverage is fairly limited. The southern half has almost nothing inland.

gu-KSIf.title: Google car: fully blurred, antenna and rack
gu-KSIf.summary: The whole car is blurred, but you can see an antenna at the front right and a small bit of roof rack. The Northern Mariana Islands car has no roof rack.

differs.how: The Northern Mariana Islands car shows no roof rack

gu-a1Iu.title: Vegetation: dense, low tropical growth
gu-a1Iu.summary: Tropical climate with dense, fairly low vegetation.

gu-eTI3.title: Language: Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian
gu-eTI3.summary: East Asian languages like Japanese, Chinese and Korean, and even Russian, are common on signs. The Northern Mariana Islands are the same.

gu-hxXB.title: Sign: yellow signposts near a resort town
gu-hxXB.summary: Some signposts near the town of Apra View are painted yellow.

gu-qvj3.title: Landscape: hills in the southern half
gu-qvj3.summary: Hills are mostly found in the southern half of the island.

gu-w6da.title: Territory: counts as the US for streaks
gu-w6da.summary: This is a US overseas territory, so for country streaks it counts as the US.
